financial_tie.text: Keytruda Qlex was $395M of $5,006M U.S. Keytruda-family sales in Q2 2026 (7.9%). Because Medicare pays a small per-dose premium for Qlex rather than a discount (+3.6% that quarter), each U.S. patient converted keeps or slightly raises Merck's Medicare drug revenue per dose, so the conversion is a revenue defense, not a price concession, ahead of the December 2028 compound-patent expiry. This ties to the c10 pricing note and to the Halozyme finding above (the block on the same product in Europe).

Q2 2026 drug payment per dose: Qlex 395[1][3] mg x $32.129[assumption] = $12,691[derived: assumption]; IV 200[4] mg x $61.251[assumption] = $12,250[derived: assumption]; 12,691[derived: assumption] / 12,250[derived: assumption] - 1 = 3.6%[derived: assumption].

evidence.finding: Zero analyst turns name the NOPAs, the transition tax, TCJA or the IRS across the 10 covered calls (2024Q1 to 2026Q2), and a full-text search of every indexed MRK transcript, release and slide deck finds no mention by management either. Limiter: Qlex or subcutaneous Keytruda was raised by analysts on calls from 2024Q1 to 2025Q4 but on neither 2026 call (topic top_products is asked every quarter).

No item-level GDELT query exists for the IRS NOPAs or for Qlex. Nearest proxy "Merck" (Keytruda OR Januvia) spiked in the Q2 reporting month (2026-07: [figure withheld: not gated], 2026-08: [figure withheld: not gated], 2026-09: [figure withheld: not gated] articles), which reflects Keytruda news generally, not the tax item. Raw table, not re-verified; context only.

Company-level FY2026 mean EPS consensus was unchanged and revenue consensus moved up slightly between the snapshots before and after the Q2 10-Q (2026-07-16 to 2026-08-20). Direction only. The NOPAs would hit GAAP tax and cash, not the non-GAAP EPS the Street models, so consensus would not show them even if known.

Two-day abnormal returns were small and negative on both disclosures carrying the item: the FY2025 10-K ([figure withheld: not gated]) and the Q2 2026 10-Q (-0.4%), each filed apart from the earnings release.
